reason: Lewitus et al. 2014 Table S1 neocortex is not a Lewitus measurement. It is the Stephan-collection volume republished: 28 of 33 values are EXACT matches to Stephan et al. 1981 Tables V-VI, Frahm et al. 1982 Table 2, or de Sousa et al. 2010 Suppl. Table 2 (Stephan 1981 Table VI is exact on all 11 species it covers). Taking it would republish Stephan/Frahm under a 2014 date. Three further defects make the column unusable rather than merely redundant: (1) MIS-CITED SOURCE - External Database S1 attributes the column to ref (17) Bush & Allman 2003 on 23 of 25 rows, but Bush & Allman match none of the 66 testable species x compartment rows (e.g. Aotus trivirgatus printed 9950 vs Bush & Allman 1.49+4.32 cm3 = 5810). (2) MIS-STATED ANATOMY - Table S2 defines the variable as neocortex MINUS corpus callosum, but the values equal the cc-INCLUSIVE Stephan/Frahm totals to the digit (Stephan code 18 footnote 18; Frahm 1982 Methods p.376), and no grey-only or white-only compartment matches anywhere (0 of 92 testable split-compartment rows). (3) UNIT ERROR - Nycticebus coucang is printed 6.192 where Frahm gives 6192 mm3, a missed cm3->mm3 conversion. Superseding alone was insufficient: 5 species carry undocumented species_sci re-identifications in this trait table (Aotus trivirgatus->nancymaae, Otolemur crassicaudatus->garnettii, Saimiri sciureus->boliviensis boliviensis, Gorilla gorilla->gorilla gorilla gorilla, Galagoides->Galago demidoff) that are absent from _keys/reidentifications.csv, so they do not collide with the merge species and slipped past the supersede into the app under the canonical Neocortex_Vol.mm3 label.

Zero-fallback duplicate of __merging_gyrification. The Lewitus et al. 2014 Table S1/S8 GI column was superseded onto the merge label GI by _keys/variable_canonical.csv, but the supersede leaves a column in the melt as a fallback for species the merge lacks, and here there are none: all 102 species the melt carries are covered by gyrification_long.csv (which adds Zilles et al. 2013 for 15 further species). The melt therefore contributed 102 rows the app discarded at startup, and on the 6 species where the merge prefers Zilles the melt was re-exposing the superseded Lewitus value up to the point of discard. Dropping it upstream makes the intent visible in the build rather than only in the app's startup logic. The variable_canonical.csv GI row is kept for the record and now matches nothing.

Zero-fallback duplicate of __merging_body_ecology (life_history class). All 101 species in the melt are covered by body_ecology_long.csv, so the supersede in _keys/variable_canonical.csv never falls back and the 101 melted rows are discarded at startup. Same treatment as the other Lewitus life-history columns would be wrong: Gestation_days, Weaning_period_days, Female_sexual_maturity_days, Maximum_lifespan_yrs, Body_weight, Brain_weight_g, Basal_metabolic_rate and Ventricle_mm^3 each still carry species the merge lacks, so those stay in the melt under supersede-plus-fallback.

Zero-fallback duplicate of __merging_body_ecology (diet_ecology class). Diet_breadth reached the app from two melted trait files at once (diet_foraging.xlsx 197 rows, glia_gyrification.xlsx 95) on top of the merge; diet_foraging.xlsx is no longer melted at all (build_data.R section 2) and this row removes the second path. All 95 Lewitus species are covered by body_ecology_long.csv. NB the neighbouring Lewitus column '% Fruit and seeds' is NOT dropped: it is a combined fruit+seed percentage that Wilman partitions into Diet_Fruit + Diet_Seed, and variable_canonical.csv adjudicates it keep_separate.
